lessons.title: Introductions and belonging
objectives: Introduce yourself and identify people or organizations.
Use は, も, and の in simple noun sentences.

grammar.meaning: A is B
grammar.usage: Use は to mark the topic and です for a polite noun predicate.

example.japanese: わたしは りさです。
example.reading: Watashi wa Risa desu.

grammar.meaning: A is also B
grammar.usage: も replaces は when the second subject has the same predicate.

example.japanese: たなかさんも せんせいです。
example.reading: Tanaka-san mo sensei desu.
example.translation: Mr./Ms. Tanaka is also a teacher.

grammar.meaning: N2 of N1; N1's N2
grammar.usage: Link two nouns to show belonging, category, or affiliation.

example.japanese: これは にほんごの ほんです。
example.reading: Kore wa nihongo no hon desu.

lessons.title: Objects and demonstratives
objectives: Identify nearby and distant objects.
Use これ, それ, あれ and この, その, あの.

grammar.pattern: これ／それ／あれ は N です
grammar.meaning: This/that over there is N
grammar.usage: Use standalone demonstratives when the noun is understood or omitted.

example.japanese: それは じしょです。
example.reading: Sore wa jisho desu.

grammar.meaning: This/that N
grammar.usage: Use these before a noun; the distance follows the same three-way pattern.

example.japanese: あの かさは わたしのです。
example.reading: Ano kasa wa watashi no desu.
example.translation: That umbrella over there is mine.

grammar.pattern: そうです／そうではありません
grammar.meaning: That is right / That is not right
grammar.usage: Use as a short confirmation or correction.

example.japanese: はい、そうです。
example.reading: Hai, sou desu.

lessons.title: Places and directions
objectives: Ask where a place or object is.
Use polite place words and direction expressions.

grammar.usage: Use は for the topic and a place noun as the predicate.

example.japanese: としょかんは あそこです。

grammar.meaning: This way/person; that way/person
grammar.usage: Use the polite direction forms for places or people.

lessons.title: Time and daily schedules
objectives: Tell the time and state when activities occur.
Use に, から, and まで with time expressions.

grammar.meaning: N is at time
grammar.usage: State the time for an event.

example.japanese: いま しちじです。
example.reading: Ima shichiji desu.

grammar.meaning: Do V at time
grammar.usage: に marks a specific time.

example.japanese: ろくじに おきます。
example.reading: Rokuji ni okimasu.

grammar.pattern: time から time まで
grammar.meaning: from time to time
grammar.usage: Use with schedules and durations.

example.japanese: くじから ごじまで はたらきます。
example.reading: Kuji kara goji made hatarakimasu.
example.translation: I work from nine to five.

bunkei.japanese: いま くじはんです。
bunkei.reading: Ima kuji han desu.
bunkei.translation: It is half past nine now.

bunkei.japanese: まいあさ ろくじに おきます。
bunkei.reading: Maiasa rokuji ni okimasu.
bunkei.translation: I get up at six every morning.

bunkei.japanese: ぎんこうは くじから さんじまでです。
bunkei.reading: Ginkou wa kuji kara sanji made desu.
bunkei.translation: The bank is open from nine to three.

reibun.response: じゅういちじに ねます。

reibun.translation: What time do you go to bed? I go to bed at eleven.

reibun.response: げつようびから きんようびまでです。
reibun.reading: Itsu hatarakimasu ka. Getsuyoubi kara kinyoubi made desu.
reibun.translation: When do you work? From Monday through Friday.

lessons.title: Going places
objectives: State destinations and means of transportation.
Ask when and with whom someone travels.

grammar.pattern: place へ いきます／きます／かえります
grammar.meaning: Go/come/return to a place
grammar.usage: へ marks the direction or destination of movement.

example.japanese: らいしゅう おおさかへ いきます。
example.reading: Raishuu Oosaka e ikimasu.
example.translation: I will go to Osaka next week.

grammar.meaning: Do V by vehicle
grammar.usage: で marks the means of transportation.

example.japanese: でんしゃで かいしゃへ いきます。
example.reading: Densha de kaisha e ikimasu.
example.translation: I go to the company by train.

grammar.meaning: Do V with a person
grammar.usage: と marks a companion.

example.japanese: ともだちと えいがを みます。
example.reading: Tomodachi to eiga o mimasu.
example.translation: I watch a movie with a friend.
